“Applicable Liquidity Threshold” means $37.5 million; provided
that to the extent that, as of any date of determination, the maximum committed amount of the Super-Senior Revolving Facility (or any Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof) is increased in excess of $62.0 million (such excess amount, the
“RCF Increase Amount”), the Applicable Liquidity Threshold shall be increased by an amount equal to 26.0% of the RCF Increase Amount up to a maximum Applicable Liquidity Threshold not to exceed $50.0 million.

“Applicable Rate” means a percentage per annum equal to (i) until delivery of the financial statements for the first
full fiscal quarter ending after the Closing Date pursuant to Section 6.01, (A) 8.00% for Term Benchmark Loans, and (B) 7.00% for Base Rate Loans and (ii) thereafter, the following percentages per annum, based upon the Secured Net Leverage
Ratio as specified in the most recent Compliance Certificate received by the Administrative Agent pursuant to Section 6.02(1):

Any increase or decrease in the Applicable Rate resulting from a change in the Secured Net Leverage Ratio
shall become effective as of the first Business Day immediately following the date a Compliance Certificate is delivered pursuant to Section 6.02(1); provided that, at the option of the Required Facility Lenders, “Pricing
Level 1” (as set forth above) shall apply as of (x) the first Business Day after the date on which a Compliance Certificate was required to have been delivered but was not delivered, and shall continue to so apply to and including the
date on which such Compliance Certificate is so delivered (and thereafter the pricing level otherwise determined in accordance with this definition shall apply) or (y) the first Business Day after an Event of Default under Section 8.01(1)
shall have occurred and be continuing, and shall continue to so apply to but excluding the date on which such Event of Default is cured or waived (and thereafter the pricing level otherwise determined in accordance with this definition shall apply).

“Appropriate Lender” means, at any time, with respect to Loans of any Class, the Lenders of such Class.

“Approved Fund” means, with respect to any Lender, any Fund that is administered, advised or managed by (a) such Lender,
(b) an Affiliate of such Lender or (c) an entity or an Affiliate of an entity that administers, advises or manages such Lender.

“Asset Sale” means:

(1) the sale, conveyance, transfer or other disposition, whether in a single transaction or a series of related transactions of
property or assets of the Borrower or any Subsidiary of the Borrower (each referred to in this definition as a “disposition”); or

(2) the issuance or sale of Equity Interests (other than Preferred Stock or Disqualified Stock of Subsidiaries issued in
compliance with Section 7.02 and directors’ qualifying shares or shares or interests required to be held by foreign nationals or other third parties to the extent required by applicable Law) of any Subsidiary (other than to the Borrower or
another Subsidiary), whether in a single transaction or a series of related transactions;

4

in each case, other than:

(a) any disposition of:

(i) Cash Equivalents or Investment Grade Securities,

(ii) obsolete, damaged or worn out property or assets in the ordinary course of business or consistent with industry practice
or any disposition of inventory or goods (or other assets) held for sale or no longer used or useful in the ordinary course,

(iii) [reserved],

(iv) improvements made to leased real property to landlords pursuant to customary terms of leases entered into in the ordinary
course of business and
(v) assets for purposes of charitable contributions or similar gifts to the extent such assets are
not material to the ability of the Borrower and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, to conduct its business in the ordinary course;

(b) the disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of the Borrower in a manner permitted pursuant to
Section 7.03 (other than Section 7.03(6) or Section 7.03(7));
(c) any disposition in connection with the
making of any Restricted Payment that is permitted to be made, and is made, under Section 7.05, any Permitted Investment or any acquisition otherwise permitted under this Agreement;

(d) any disposition of property or assets or issuance or sale of Equity Interests of any Subsidiary with an aggregate fair
market value for any individual transaction or series of related transactions of an amount (i) equal to or greater than $500,000 and less than $5.0 million, but not in excess of $20 million in the aggregate for all such transactions

findings.sourceEvidence: "Applicable Rate" means a percentage per annum equal to (i) until delivery of the financial statements for the first full fiscal quarter ending after the Closing Date pursuant to Section 6.01, (A) 8.00% for Term Benchmark Loans, and (B) 7.00% for Base Rate Loans and (ii) thereafter, the following percentages per annum, based upon the Secured Net Leverage Ratio...
findings.proposedIrEvidence: calculationExpression.kind = "UNSUPPORTED" at the top level of the Applicable Rate definition, with every nested branch (then/else of every IF, and the OR condition) also resolving to kind "UNSUPPORTED" with requiredReview:true, because the TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE and EVENT_ACTIVE nodes were typed MONEY instead of BOOLEAN so no IF condition ever type-checks; sufficiency is nonetheless recorded as "PARTIAL".
findings.verifierReasoning: The root calculationExpression for Applicable Rate is itself kind=UNSUPPORTED, and every single descendant IF/OR node in the tree is also UNSUPPORTED due to a type-checking failure (condition typed MONEY rather than BOOLEAN). This means there is no path through this expression tree that ever resolves to an actual PERCENT value - the correct-looking 8.00%/7.00%/7.75%/6.75%/7.50%/6.50% figures and the 1.00/0.50 ratio breakpoints only exist inside inert 'attemptedStructure' debug metadata, not in any live/reachable branch of the compiled expression. Labeling this definition's sufficiency as PARTIAL materially overstates its usability: PARTIAL implies a mostly-working representation with some gaps, but in fact zero percentage values are computable from this IR as written. A downstream consumer relying on the sufficiency flag could wrongly conclude a workable (if incomplete) Applicable Rate formula exists, when none does. This is a genuine, testable discrepancy between what the source clearly and unambiguously specifies (a complete, well-defined tiered-rate mechanism) and what the proposed IR actually delivers (nothing computable).

findings.sourceEvidence: "provided that, at the option of the Required Facility Lenders, "Pricing Level 1" (as set forth above) shall apply as of (x) the first Business Day after the date on which a Compliance Certificate was required to have been delivered but was not delivered... or (y) the first Business Day after an Event of Default under Section 8.01(1) shall have occurred and be continuing..."
findings.proposedIrEvidence: The attempted structure represents the failure-to-deliver and continuing-Event-of-Default triggers as an unconditional OR of two EVENT_ACTIVE nodes that, if true, automatically force Pricing Level 1 (8.00%/7.00%), with no representation anywhere of the source's express qualifier that this override applies only "at the option of the Required Facility Lenders."
findings.verifierReasoning: The source makes the Pricing Level 1 override for a missed Compliance Certificate or a continuing Event of Default an elective right of the Required Facility Lenders, not an automatic consequence - the lenders must choose to invoke it. The (non-functional) attempted structure in the proposed IR nonetheless models this as an automatic OR-triggered override with no election/discretion mechanism at all. Even setting aside that the whole branch is currently UNSUPPORTED, the conceptual model omits an independently operative condition (lender election) that changes the real-world outcome: under the actual contract, if the Required Facility Lenders do not elect to invoke the override, Pricing Level 1 does not automatically apply merely because a certificate was late or a default is continuing, whereas the modeled structure would force it automatically. This is a substantive logical-grouping/condition omission distinct from, and in addition to, the broader UNSUPPORTED-rooted defect.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: METRIC_REFERENCE metricName "Super-Senior Revolving Facility Maximum Committed Amount (or Refinancing Indebtedness thereof)" uses instrumentKey "sup-term-loan-instrument", the same instrumentKey also used elsewhere for the unrelated "Secured Net Leverage Ratio" metric (which is naturally tied to the term loan facility itself).
findings.verifierReasoning: The metric being referenced is explicitly the committed amount of the Super-Senior Revolving Facility (a different facility from the term loan this agreement otherwise appears keyed to), yet the instrumentKey used to resolve it ("sup-term-loan-instrument") textually suggests a term-loan instrument rather than the revolving facility. If instrumentKey in this system is meant to identify the specific facility a metric is measured against (rather than merely tagging the overall deal/document), this could point the Applicable Liquidity Threshold's RCF-increase calculation at the wrong facility's committed-amount figure, which would produce an incorrect threshold. I cannot confirm from the material given whether instrumentKey is deal-level or facility-level, so I flag this as uncertain rather than a confirmed error.
